searches.note: Twenty six searches of a share of twenty eight, none the author's. Eleven were restricted to a producer's or a federal body's domain (drfrankwines.com three times, wiemer.com twice, ravineswine.com three times, boundarybreaks.com twice, forgecellars.com twice, ttb.gov) and read as primary for the house's own facts; one was restricted to Wikipedia. No WebFetch was tried.

method: Each record was read with one instruction, refute it: the founding year, the people and their dates, the grapes, the sites, the making, the drinking window, the serving temperature, the label words, every beat of the story, the cards and the questions; then the house rules.
What a search contradicted was set right with its source; what rested on no source found was cut; every glass note was held against tasting notes found and rewritten where they disagreed.

tested: Founder's dates 1899 to 1985, Odessa, the doctorate in viticulture, Ellis Island 1951: Wikipedia and a second biographical summary; one Russian source gives 1897.
Gold Seal: the house's story page dates the meeting and hiring to 1953; Wikipedia gives the partnership but no year.
Land 1958 and founding 1962: the house's homepage and sales packet; 1957 in one listing.
The son's sparkling property: 1980 on most of the house's pages, 1982 on one; first sparkling 1985.

Dry Riesling: the house's sheets of 2018, 2019, 2022, 2023 and 2024 (steel, cool, no oak, no malolactic, Keuka blocks from 1958, Seneca from 2007, 5.7 to 8.5 g/l sugar); tasting notes of 2015, 2018, 2023, 2024 and 2025.
Eugenia planted 1968: the house's page and the 2023 sheet.
Finger Lakes AVA 1982 and Seneca Lake 2003: TTB's list of establishment dates.
changed: story: was 'met the president of Gold Seal ... and from 1954 the two made experimental plantings'; now he met the head of Gold Seal in 1953, who hired him that year by the house's account, and together they planted, since the house's own story page dates the hiring to 1953 and Wikipedia gives no year.
story: was the son's sparkling property bought in 1980; now the early 1980s, since the house's own pages give 1980 and 1982.
questions: the story stem now says the 1950s and the explanation the hiring of 1953, by the house's account.
wine.sites: was a Seneca vineyard 'a few degrees warmer'; now the Seneca vineyard planted from 2007, as the 2024 sheet gives it, the warmth claim having no source.
wine.making: 'with selected yeasts' cut, found on no sheet read; steel, cool fermentation, no oak, no malolactic and five months on lees (2019) confirmed by the sheets of 2018 to 2024.
wine.glass: rewritten from the house's notes of 2015, 2018, 2023 and 2024 (lime, grapefruit, apricot, petrol stoniness); green apple and slate dropped.
wine.label: Dry Riesling now 'dry to the taste, with only a few grams of sugar left', since the sheets give 5.7 to 8.5 grams a litre.
open: The founder's birth year is 1897 in one Russian source against 1899 in Wikipedia, the house and others; 1899 kept.

tested: 1968 at Bully Hill, the farm of 1973 at Dundee, founding 1979: Wikipedia, the house's archive and media kit, Wine Spectator.
First wines: the house says 1979; Wine Spectator says the first commercial vintage was 1981, after the firing from Bully Hill.
HJW site: shale, planted 1976 to 1978 (the sheet) or 1977 (the shop page); whole cluster, indigenous yeast, steel, Demeter from 2023: the house's sheet and shop page.
The founder living: a search for a death found none; Wine Spectator and Wikipedia describe him as retired.
Sugar and glass: merchants give about 7 g/l for 2017, 2022 and 2023; notes of 2019, 2022 and 2023.
changed: story: was 'His first wines ... of the 1979 vintage mark the founding'; now the house's account of a first release in 1979, with Wine Spectator's first wines for sale in 1981, after he left Bully Hill, since the two disagree.
wine.glass: crushed stone and white peach from reviews of 2022 and 2023; the rest confirmed by a review of 2022.
open: The founder is treated as living: no report of his death was found in a search for one; he is never named in prose.

The HJW Vineyard Riesling's sugar, about 6 to 7 grams a litre by merchants for 2017, 2022 and 2023, sits under the record's 'less than a per cent'; no house sheet for the bottling itself gave a figure.

tested: Founders, Provence, 1998 at Dr. Konstantin Frank, leaving in 2005: Decanter, Grape Collective, the house.
Founding: the house's sheet and Decanter give 2001; Skurnik and Prince of Pinot give 2000, the land.
First vintage 2002 and the World Riesling Cup: the house (2002 and 2003 on different pages).

Argetsinger: southeast Seneca shore below Burdett, town of Hector, Howard gravel over limestone, planted in the early 1980s, owned and operated by the Argetsinger family: the house's sheets and vineyard page, Skurnik.
Making: the house's sheets of 2015 to 2021 (cool steel, fine lees through winter, stirring in 2015, about 3 g/l sugar).
changed: founded: was empty; now 2001, from the house's own sheet and Decanter, the land of 2000 kept in the story (Skurnik and another source give 2000 for the land).

story: the rented barn on Keuka Lake, the move of 2010 and the renaming of the Geneva site as Limestone Springs found no source and are cut; the move to Geneva is kept without a year (Decanter, the house's tasting rooms).
story: was 16 Falls drawn on 'from the start'; now 16 Falls and White Springs follow from 2003 and 2004, the house's own planting years.
story: was the Argetsinger Vineyard 'managed by Ravines'; now owned and farmed by the Argetsinger family, as the house's own vineyard page says; the label term and trap follow.
story: the World Riesling Cup prize is now told as the house tells it, without a year, since its own pages give 2002 and 2003.
story and question: the winemaker's post at Dr. Konstantin Frank is now head winemaker, 1998 to 2005, from Decanter and the house's own page.
wine.sites and table: the planting in the early 1980s added from the house's sheet and the importer's listing.

sources: Life in the Finger Lakes gives way to Skurnik.
open: The Argetsinger family members named on the house's pages are not named; whether the elder is living was not settled.

tested: History: the house's own history page (Covert 1861, rented after 1967, the cabin, the sale of 2008) and FAQ (founded 2008, planting 2009).
Clones: the house's sheets (five clones in 2009, 239 slightly more acidic, steel) and one article (90, 198, 239).
First release 2013: the house; a No. 239 of 2012 is listed by a merchant, consistent with it.
changed: founded: was empty; now 2008, from the house's FAQ and the Finger Lakes Wine Alliance.

story: the deep ripping of the soil, the vines from a California nursery, the harvest of 2011 and clone 110 found no source and are cut; the first release of 2013 is the house's own; the Covert tenure to 1967 added from the house's history.
questions: the story key was 'No vines and a half built cabin'; now 'Only a half built cabin', since the house names the cabin as the only building and says nothing of vines.
wine.sites and wine.making: the heavy deep ripped soil and bottling in the year after harvest cut for want of a source; steel fermentation confirmed by the sheets of 2015 to 2022.
wine.glass: was lime, tangerine, flint and ginger, found in no note; now key lime, lemon peel, apple, crushed stone, verbena and white peach, from notes of 2012, 2018, 2019 and 2023.

open: One article lists the clones as 90, 198 and 239 against the house's five clones of 2009; the record names only 198 and 239.
The label form No. 239 against the house's own Riesling Dry 239 is left as the plan has it; merchants print No. 239 Dry Riesling.

Railroad and the Lehigh Valley ties: Decanter; glass from reviews quoted on the house's pages (2013, 2015, 2023).

wine.making: fermentation in neutral barrels is now 'in the vintages read', with some steel in earlier years, since the 2021 and 2023 pages give neutral barrel and a 2017 listing a share in steel; the table follows.

story: 'sits high above Burdett' cut to 'is at Burdett', the address on the house's sheet; the Railroad site and the Lehigh Valley ties added from Decanter; the Seneca Lake appellation of 2003 added as a dated turning point from TTB.
wine.glass: was plum, lemon oil, grapefruit and salt; now Mirabelle plum, bergamot, lemon zest, chamomile and apple skin from reviews of 2013, 2015 and 2023 quoted by the house.

livingNamesNote: None is written in the fragment; the names are for the read-together agent to add to people.json, which this lane does not edit.
swapNote: The author proposed no swap; the five picks stand. The author's suggestion that the integrator reorder Forge's wine to the label's form, Dry Riesling Classique, is a rename for the integrator, not a swap; the refuter agrees the label reads that way on the house's pages.
questions: All ten questions were read: one key each, four options of one kind, the key never the longest by much and never in the stem; two explanations rewritten (Dr. Konstantin Frank's story, Forge's wine) and one key reworded (Boundary Breaks' story) to match what the sources say.
codexTension: The library record p-hermann-j-wiemer's third trap names two living people (the winemaker and partner of 2007), as the author reported; reported, not edited.
The library record p-hermann-j-wiemer's why calls its dry Rieslings 'the region's benchmark' in the region producers line, a judging word the flagship rules refuse; reported, not edited.
The region summary says Wiemer 'followed on Seneca in 1979'; the house gives 1979 and Wine Spectator 1981 for the first wines sold, so the summary holds on the house's account.
